overview: This file centers on a 1940 U.S. consular study of Japan’s silk industry, covering cocoon farming, production, trade, prices, government controls, and competing fibers. Related correspondence evaluates the study; later documents address wartime silk use and proposed Japanese fur seal hunting.
interest: Detailed tables and charts pair with officials’ assessments of silk prices, controls, and wartime use.
